beats.text: A traffic spike hits your service.
beats.say: What happens when requests arrive faster than your service can handle them?

beats.text: Overloaded, blocked, and requests get lost.
beats.say: The service gets overloaded, slow jobs block the caller, and when it crashes, requests are lost.

beats.text: A queue sits in between: producers drop messages, consumers pick them up.
beats.say: A message queue sits in between. Producers drop messages in, and consumers pick them up when they're ready.
The producer never waits. It hands off the message and moves on, even during a huge spike.

beats.text: Consumers pull at their own pace. Need speed? Add consumers.
beats.say: Consumers pull messages at their own pace, which smooths out the spike. Need more speed? Just add more consumers.

beats.text: A crash doesn't lose the message: it's retried.
beats.say: And if a consumer crashes mid-job, the message isn't lost. It goes back in the queue, and another consumer retries it.
